verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const fsx=["components/vera/vera-chat.tsx","components/onboarding/vera-lightbox.tsx"];for(const f of fsx){if(!fs.existsSync(f))process.exit(79);const T=fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8");if(/\n\s*await confirmProposal\(/.test(T)){console.error("SCAN-739: "+f+" still discards the result of confirmProposal, so a refused Vera proposal (no consent, full circle, unknown handle) vanishes as if it worked.");process.exit(1)}}'

append.detail: Both Vera surfaces (components/vera/vera-chat.tsx and components/onboarding/vera-lightbox.tsx) removed the proposal card and then awaited confirmProposal as a bare statement, so a { ok: false, error } from the server (no memory consent, full circle, unknown handle, not signed in) was discarded and the card vanished as if the write had happened. allow() now reads the result: on !ok it puts the card back and appends the server's reason as a Vera bubble inside the role=log live region; a thrown action rejection is caught and shown as a plain line. A join_circle success redirects from the action and resolves with nothing on the client, which is left alone. Pinned by components/vera/vera-proposal-refusal.test.tsx, which mounts both surfaces, offers a proposal through a mocked stream, taps Allow, and asserts the refused card returns with the reason in the transcript, the thrown case shows the fallback line, and a success leaves the card gone with no extra bubble.
